title: In a 2020 plant assembly experiment, the main biomass winner had earlier modal but later median germination
abstract: We tested whether a warming-derived plant arrival schedule favoured species with higher germination yield under warmth. We used an independent experiment with 15 species, 24 greenhouse pots and separate 2019 seed records. Rumex crispus gained 31.7 percentage points of biomass share in the warm schedule (95% pot bootstrap interval 23.1 to 40.0). Its modal germination was 19 days earlier in the warm tray, but its median was 3 days later and its mean was 10.8 days later. Only 7 warm-tray seeds germinated, compared with 11 ambient-tray seeds. The biomass-weighted yield-response score fell by 0.0296 (pot interval -0.0464 to -0.0120). A conditional seed-count sensitivity interval crossed zero (-0.0905 to 0.0289), and removal of Rumex reversed the point estimate. Thus the measured biomass response did not establish a general benefit to species with positive thermal yield responses. The source study already showed arrival-order effects and the benefit to Rumex. We add a timing-measure audit, a separate yield diagnostic and uncertainty checks. One tray per species and treatment, sparse seed counts, selected species and common growth temperature limit inference. This result does not measure climate niches or explain a share of the field thermal-tracking gap. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Rumex germination records give opposite modal and median timing contrasts. Seed-count uncertainty removes a clear sign from a biomass-weighted yield-response diagnostic.

citations.reason: Weak species exchange motivates an independent experiment after species arrival.
Weak annual transfer in river communities motivates tests that distinguish community change from thermal direction.
Source experiment already showed composition and Rumex biomass effects. We add yield and timing-measure checks, not the discovery of arrival-order effects.
